sources.quote: roughly 46 percent of Canadians used a generative AI tool in the past year, up from 33 percent in 2025 and 16 percent in 2024
sources.title: 2026 Canadian Internet Trends – CIRA
sources.evidence: Nearly half of respondents (46 per cent) say they have used a generative AI tool or platform in the past year, up from 33 per cent in 2025 and 16 per cent in 2024. Canadians are primarily turning to generative AI as a search engine (52 per cent) and for experimentation (42 per cent).

sources.quote: people clicked a traditional result 8 percent of the time against 15 percent without one
sources.title: Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears in the results
sources.evidence: Users who landed on a Google search page with an AI summary clicked on a search result 8% of the time, while those who did not encounter an AI summary clicked on a search result 15% of the time. The total dataset used in this analysis contains 68,879 unique Google searches, from 900 U.S. adults who agreed to share their online browsing activity, with data collected from March 1-31, 2025.

sources.quote: Google's AI optimization guidance states that no special schema.org markup is required for AI Overviews or AI Mode, and that ordinary search fundamentals are the requirement
sources.title: AI Features and Your Website | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary. There's no special schema.org structured data that you need to add. All existing SEO fundamentals continue to be worthwhile, for example: Ensuring that crawling is allowed in robots.txt.

sources.quote: Google's guidance now states that Search ignores the file
sources.title: Google's Guide to Optimizing for Generative AI Features on Google Search | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, markup, or Markdown to appear in Google Search (including its generative AI capabilities), as Google Search itself doesn't use them. It's completely fine if you decide to create and maintain LLMS.txt files for other services or systems that use these files. Doing so will neither harm nor help your site's visibility or rankings in Google Search, as Google Search ignores them.

sources.quote: Google restricted FAQ rich results to well-known government and health sites in August 2023
sources.title: Changes to HowTo and FAQ rich results | Google Search Central Blog | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: The FAQ structured data documentation was updated to state that the feature is only shown for well-known, authoritative government and health websites.

sources.quote: then retired them from Search on 7 May 2026
sources.title: Latest Google Search Documentation Updates | Google Search Central | What's new | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: A deprecation notice was added to the FAQ rich result documentation, as this feature will no longer appear in Google Search starting May 7, 2026. Google removed documentation for the FAQ rich result feature because it is no longer shown in Google Search results, as announced in May 2026.

sources.quote: Google added a native AI Assistant channel to GA4's Default Channel Group, tagging qualifying sessions with the medium ai-assistant
sources.title: Default channel group - Analytics Help
sources.evidence: Google Analytics now automatically assigns a new ai-assistant value to the Medium dimension when the referrer matches a recognized AI Assistant, and these visits are categorized under the AI Assistant channel in the Default Channel Group reports.

sources.quote: Search Console added generative AI performance reporting in June 2026, fully rolled out by the end of August
sources.title: Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console | Google Search Central Blog | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: Google has launched new Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console, including dedicated reports for Search and Discover, giving dedicated views of impressions within generative AI features on Search, such as AI Overviews and AI Mode. As of August 31, 2026, these insights have been rolled out to all websites worldwide. Impressions are how many times links to your site were shown to a user in a generative AI feature on Google Search.

flags.quote: Claude and Perplexity are not on that list and still land in generic Referral
flags.issue: Google's Default channel group documentation lists Claude and Perplexity among the recognized AI assistants whose referrals are assigned the ai-assistant medium and the AI Assistant channel (examples given: ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Claude, Perplexity), so they do not fall into generic Referral.
